words.where: Mexico, Argentina, Uruguay, much of Central America

note: Means to fuck. In the Caribbean, Colombia and Spain it's a harmless word for take or grab, so people from those places often get caught out. Use tomar or agarrar.
Means penis. Everywhere else it's just a bug or a critter, so this one surprises a lot of visitors.
Slang for female genitals, which is why Cubans say fruta bomba for the fruit.
Slang for female genitals. Concha de tu madre is a strong insult. Elsewhere it's a seashell, and in Mexico also a sweet bread.

words.where: Cuba, Puerto Rico, Dominican Republic, Venezuela, Spain

note: Literally female genitals. In practice it's a very common swear word for surprise or anger, like damn or fuck. It's in everyday speech but still rude in polite company.
Slang for female genitals, and ¡chucha! works as an exclamation. In Colombia it means armpit odor instead.
Means penis. Vete a la verga is roughly fuck off, and ¡verga! alone is a strong exclamation.
Means penis. In Cuba, de pinga can mean either awesome or awful, depending on tone.
Means penis. Elsewhere it's a beak or a peak. Chileans say hora punta rather than hora pico for rush hour.
Means penis. In Chile and Colombia it's a betting pool or lottery, so context matters.
Means penis. In Spain, pijo and pija describe a snobby rich kid, which isn't vulgar.
Means to fuck, and it's the root of a whole family of Mexican swearing. Chingada is a strong insult, while chingón means awesome and is much milder.
Means no way or you're kidding. It's very common among friends, but mamar refers to oral sex here, so don't say it to your boss or your in-laws. No manches is the clean version.
Literally to fuck. In Spain it's an everyday swear word. In the Caribbean, no jodas is closer to quit messing around, or no way. It's milder there, but still not polite.
Means whore. It's an insult aimed at someone's mother or at women, which is why it hits hard. ¡Puta! alone is also an exclamation.
Literally a big male goat, with an old sense of a man whose wife cheats on him. It means bastard, but among close male friends it can mean dude. Tone decides, so don't try it yourself.
Literally a pubic hair. It means idiot, and it's stronger than tonto. In Argentina it just means a kid, and is much milder.
Both come from words for testicles and mean idiot. Among friends they're also the everyday word for dude, so you'll hear them constantly. With strangers they're an insult.
Culo means ass and mierda means shit. They carry about the same weight as the English words, and both are understood everywhere.

words.where: everywhere, with a casual sense in Colombia

note: A slur against gay men, and offensive in the same way as its English equivalents. Colombian friends may call each other marica to mean dude, but that doesn't make it safe for a learner to copy. Say gay or homosexual.
